RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

The panel's gender composition alone is not evidence of discrimination; it typically reflects staff availability or department leadership demographics. For a department head role, formal management training and broad leadership experience often outweigh an advanced research degree like a PhD. 

Accusing the panel of bias based solely on their gender is legally unsubstantiated and risks severely damaging your professional reputation and relationships within the hospital network. 

Instead, send a polite follow-up inquiry regarding your feedback request, framing it constructively around identifying skill gaps or leadership areas to develop. Only consider consulting an employment specialist if you uncover concrete evidence of procedural irregularities or overt bias, rather than demographic assumptions.
